what: argon2_fill one-cycle write-back: block cost, area, and the full-size engine
machine: 56-core Xeon (airobots@192.168.1.15) for Verilator; local x86-64 for yosys and Icarus

change.before: out[64*f +: 64] written one word per cycle, f = gcnt - 128, 128 cycles for the write-back
change.after: a for loop writes all 128 words in the single cycle where gcnt == 128
change.why_it_was_half_the_block: the permutation is 128 G operations, one per cycle; the write-back serialised the other 128 words, so a block cost 128 + 128 plus a handshake cycle

measured_full_size.how: make vlreal (Verilator 5.020, M_COST=19456, DIFF=5) in an isolated server tree

yosys_generic_cells.why: the serialised form indexed out[64*f +: 64] with the register f, so yosys built a 128-way 8192-bit mux plus its feedback; with a constant index each word is only an XOR tree

regression_checks.tb_argon2_fill: PASS - two independent blocks run back to back with start asserted on the cycle done is seen (zero idle cycles), both match gen_argon_vectors.py
regression_checks.tb_argon2_engine: PASS - whole Argon2id hashes match argon2-cffi, 3 cases
regression_checks.full suite: PASS - 14 of 14 testbenches under make -j16 sim (Icarus Verilog 12.0)

notes: the link ceiling is unchanged, so the win is half the die for the same throughput, or twice the throughput once more bandwidth is added

an earlier attempt at this same change failed tb_argon2_engine with a wrong digest; the failure was not reproduced once the boundary was made explicit (gcnt < 128 for the permutation, gcnt == 128 for the write-back) and the testbench gained a second, independent block
